sources: 1763: one stage coach a month from Edinburgh to London, 12–14 days; about 1830: six or seven coaches a day, about 48 hours. All the Year Round (Dickens' magazine), vol. VI, p. 302. 1829: the North Mail London→Edinburgh in about 43.5 hours. The Spectator, 11 July 1829, 'The North Mail'.

The lovers are illustrative. London–Edinburgh ≈ 400 miles by road; overnight stops at inns on 18th-century stage-coach journeys. Film: 'Fast Mail, Northern Pacific R.R.' (Edison, 1897), public domain, illustrative (Internet Archive).
John Palmer's mail coaches from 1784 (first run Bristol–London), horses changed at stages, armed Royal Mail guard: Postal Museum (UK), 'Mail coaches'.
